wd:Q96.overview: Mexico, officially the United Mexican States, is a country in North America. wd:Q774.label: Guatemala
wd:Q774.overview: Guatemala, officially the Republic of Guatemala, is a country in northern Central America. It is bordered to the north and west by Mexico, to the northeast (in the adjacency zone) by Belize, to the east by Honduras, and to the southeast by El Salvador.

background.text: It is bounded by the Pacific Ocean to the south and the Gulf of Honduras to the northeast.

The territory of modern Guatemala hosted the core of the Maya civilization, which extended across Mesoamerica; in the 16th century, most of this was conquered by the Spanish and claimed as part of the viceroyalty of New Spain.

wd:Q783.label: Honduras
wd:Q783.overview: Honduras, officially the Republic of Honduras, is a country in Central America. It is bordered to the west by Guatemala, to the southwest by El Salvador, to the southeast by Nicaragua, to the south by the Pacific Ocean at the Gulf of Fonseca, and to the north by the Gulf of Honduras, a large inlet of the Caribbean Sea.

background.text: Its capital and largest city is Tegucigalpa.
Honduras was home to several important Mesoamerican cultures, most notably the Maya, before Spanish colonization in the 16th century.

wd:Q159.overview: Russia, or the Russian Federation, is a country in Eastern Europe and North Asia. It is the largest country in the world, spanning eleven time zones and sharing land borders with fourteen countries.

background.text: With a population of over 140 million, Russia is the most populous country in Europe and the ninth-most populous in the world.
It is a highly urbanised country, with three-fourths of its population living in urban areas.

wd:Q110999040.label: full-scale Russo-Ukrainian war
wd:Q110999040.description: full-scale invasion of Ukraine by Russia starting on 24 February 2022, part of Russo-Ukrainian War
wd:Q110999040.overview: On 24 February 2022, Russia invaded Ukraine, starting the largest and deadliest war in Europe since World War II, in a major escalation of the existing war between the two countries that began when Russia attacked Ukraine in 2014. The fighting has caused hundreds of thousands of military casualties and tens of thousands of Ukrainian civilian casualties.

tech:h3 rocket.label: H3 rocket
tech:h3 rocket.overview: The H3 is a Japanese medium-lift launch vehicle developed by JAXA and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (MHI). A hydrolox-fuelled rocket, it is the successor to the H-IIA and H-IIB launch vehicles.

background.text: The H3 uses the LE-9 main engine, which was designed to be less expensive to produce as part of a broader effort to lower launch costs.

The rocket has a modular design: its first stage is powered by two or three LE-9 engines and can be fitted with zero, two, or four SRB-3 solid rocket boosters, which are also used on the Epsilon S small-lift launch vehicle.

wd:Q3381348.label: Phobos
wd:Q3381348.overview: Phobos is the innermost and larger of the two natural satellites of Mars, the other being Deimos. The two moons were discovered in 1877 by American astronomer Asaph Hall.

background.text: Phobos is named after the Greek god of fear and panic, who is the twin brother of Deimos and son of Ares (Mars).
Phobos is a small, irregularly shaped object with a mean radius of 11 km (7 mi).

topic:martian moon.label: Martian moon
topic:martian moon.overview: The two moons of Mars are Phobos and Deimos. They are irregular in shape.

facts.label: a kind of
facts.quote: Martian moon: a kind of planetary moon

background.text: Both were discovered by American astronomer Asaph Hall in August 1877 and are named after the Greek mythological twin characters Phobos (fear and panic) and Deimos (terror and dread) who accompanied their father Ares (Mars in Roman mythology, hence the name of the planet) into battle.
Compared to the Earth's Moon, the moons Phobos and Deimos are very small.

wd:Q833.label: Malaysia
wd:Q833.overview: Malaysia is a country in Southeast Asia. A federal constitutional monarchy, it consists of 13 states and three federal territories, separated by the South China Sea into two regions: Peninsular Malaysia on Mainland Southeast Asia and East Malaysia on the island of Borneo.

background.text: Peninsular Malaysia shares land and maritime borders with Thailand, as well as maritime borders with Singapore, Vietnam, and Indonesia; East Malaysia shares land borders with Brunei and Indonesia, and maritime borders with the Philippines and Vietnam.

Kuala Lumpur is the country's national capital, largest city, and the seat of the legislative branch of the federal government, while Putrajaya is the federal administrative capital, representing the seat of both the executive branch and the judicial branch of the federal government.

wd:Q7755.label: constitution
wd:Q7755.description: set of fundamental principles or established precedents according to which a state or other organization is governed
wd:Q7755.overview: A constitution, or supreme law, is the aggregate of fundamental principles or established precedents that constitute the legal basis of a polity, organization or other type of entity, and commonly determines how that entity is to be governed. When these principles are written down into a single document or set of legal documents, those documents may be said to embody a written constitution; if they are encompassed in

facts.label: is a
facts.quote: constitution: is a type of law

background.text: The constitution of the United Kingdom is a notable example of an uncodified constitution; it is instead written in numerous fundamental acts of a legislature, court cases, and treaties.
Constitutions concern different levels of organizations, from sovereign countries to companies and unincorporated associations.

wd:Q212.label: Ukraine
wd:Q212.overview: Ukraine is a country in Eastern Europe. It is the second-largest country in Europe after Russia, which borders it to the east and northeast.

background.text: Ukraine also borders Belarus to the north; Poland and Slovakia to the west; Hungary, Romania and Moldova to the southwest; and the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov to the south and southeast.
Kyiv is Ukraine's capital and largest city, followed by Kharkiv, Odesa, and Dnipro.

wd:Q3348196.label: oblast of Ukraine
wd:Q3348196.description: first level administrative division of Ukraine
wd:Q3348196.overview: An oblast (Ukrainian: область, romanized: oblast, pronounced [ˈɔblɐsʲtʲ] ; pl. області, oblasti), sometimes translated as region or province, is the main type of first-level administrative division of Ukraine. The country's territory is divided into 24 oblasts, as well as one autonomous republic and two cities with special status.

facts.label: is a
facts.value: designation for an administrative territorial entity of a single country
facts.quote: oblast of Ukraine: is a designation for an administrative territorial entity of a single country

facts.label: a kind of
facts.quote: oblast of Ukraine: a kind of region of Ukraine

background.text: As Ukraine is a unitary state, oblasts do not have much legal scope of competence other than that which is established in the Ukrainian Constitution and devolved by law.
Articles 140–146 of Chapter XI of the constitution deal directly with local authorities and their competence.

wd:Q756294.label: Autonomous Republic of Crimea
wd:Q756294.description: administrative division of Ukraine since 1992, not occupying the whole peninsula
wd:Q756294.overview: The Autonomous Republic of Crimea is a de jure administrative division of Ukraine encompassing most of Crimea that was unilaterally annexed by Russia in 2014, and is now, de facto, administered as the Republic of Crimea within the Russian Federation. The Autonomous Republic of Crimea encompasses most of the peninsula, while the City of Sevastopol (a city with special status within Ukraine) occupies the rest.

facts.label: is a
facts.quote: Autonomous Republic of Crimea: is a autonomous republic

facts.label: is a
facts.quote: Autonomous Republic of Crimea: is a region of Ukraine

background.text: The Cimmerians, Scythians, Greeks, Goths, Huns, Bulgars, Khazars, Byzantine Greeks, the state of Kievan Rus', Kipchaks, Italians, and Golden Horde Mongols and Tatars each controlled Crimea in its earlier history.
In the 13th century, it was partly controlled by the Venetians and by the Genoese, and in the late 15th century, it was partly under Polish suzerainty.

wd:Q46.label: Europe
wd:Q46.description: terrestrial continent located in north-western Eurasia
wd:Q46.overview: Europe is a continent located entirely in the Northern Hemisphere and mostly in the Eastern Hemisphere. It is bordered by the Arctic Ocean to the north, the Atlantic Ocean to the west, the Mediterranean Sea to the south, and Asia to the east.

facts.label: is a
facts.quote: Europe: is a part of the world

background.text: Europe shares the landmass of Eurasia with Asia, and of Afro-Eurasia with both Africa and Asia.
Europe is commonly considered to be separated from Asia by the watershed of the Ural Mountains, the Ural River, the Caspian Sea, the Greater Caucasus, the Black Sea, and the Turkish straits.

wd:Q1899.label: Kyiv
wd:Q1899.description: capital and largest city of Ukraine
wd:Q1899.overview: Kyiv, also spelt Kiev, is the capital and most populous city of Ukraine. Located in the north-central part of the country, it straddles both banks of the Dnieper River.

facts.label: is a
facts.quote: Kyiv: is a city or town

background.text: As of January 2022, the population of Kyiv was 2,952,301, making it the seventh-most populous city in Europe.
Kyiv is an important industrial, scientific, educational, and cultural center.

wd:Q1065.label: United Nations
wd:Q1065.overview: The United Nations (UN) is an international intergovernmental organization established by the signing of the Charter of the United Nations on 26 June 1945 with the articulated mission of maintaining international peace and security, to develop friendly relations among states, to promote international cooperation, and to serve as a centre for harmonizing the actions of states in achieving those goals. The United Natio

facts.label: is a
facts.quote: United Nations: is a intergovernmental organization

facts.label: is a
facts.quote: United Nations: is a international organization

facts.label: headquarters
facts.quote: United Nations: headquarters New York City

background.text: The UN comprises six principal organizations: General Assembly, Security Council, Economic and Social Council, International Court of Justice, Secretariat and Trusteeship Council which, together with several specialized agencies and related agencies, make up the UN System.
There is a total of 193 member states, representing nearly all of the world's sovereign states, as well as two observer states, the Holy See and the State of Palestine.

wd:Q12585.label: Latin America
wd:Q12585.description: region of the Americas where Romance languages are primarily spoken
wd:Q12585.overview: Latin America (Spanish: América Latina or Latinoamérica; Portuguese: América Latina) is the cultural region of the Americas where Romance languages are predominantly spoken, primarily Spanish and Portuguese. Since it is defined according to its cultural identity instead of its geography, Latin America includes countries from both North and South America.

facts.label: is a
facts.quote: Latin America: is a transcontinental region

facts.label: is a
facts.quote: Latin America: is a cultural region

background.text: For instance, countries from North America like Mexico, Honduras, Guatemala, etc. tend to be included.
In fact, most of the countries in Central America, South America and the Caribbean are considered Latin American countries.

wd:Q29876.label: Middle America
wd:Q29876.description: region in the mid-latitudes of the Americas, consisting of Mexico, Central America, the Caribbean islands, Colombia, Venezuela, and the Guyanas ; same as the Caribbean, extended to the Pacific coast
wd:Q29876.overview: Middle America is a subregion in the Northern Hemisphere tropics of the Americas. It usually includes Mexico, the seven countries of Central America, and the 13 island countries and 18 territories of the Caribbean.

facts.label: is a
facts.quote: Middle America: is a transcontinental region

background.text: Together with Northern America, they form the continent of North America.
Colombia and Venezuela of Caribbean South America are sometimes included in this subregion.

wd:Q49.label: North America
wd:Q49.overview: North America is a continent in the Northern and Western hemispheres. It is bordered to the north by the Arctic Ocean, to the east by the Atlantic Ocean, to the southeast by South America and the Caribbean Sea, and to the south and west by the Pacific Ocean.

background.text: North America covers an area of around 24,709,000 square kilometers (9,540,000 square miles), representing approximately 16.5% of Earth's land area and 4.8% of its total surface area.
It is the third-largest continent by size after Asia and Africa, and the fourth-largest continent by population after Asia, Africa, and Europe.

wd:Q1555.label: Guatemala City
wd:Q1555.description: capital and largest city of the Republic of Guatemala
wd:Q1555.overview: Guatemala City (Spanish: Ciudad de Guatemala), also known colloquially by the nickname Guate, is the national capital and largest city of the Republic of Guatemala. It serves as the municipal capital of the surrounding Guatemala Department.

facts.label: is a
facts.quote: Guatemala City: is a municipality of Guatemala

facts.label: located in
facts.quote: Guatemala City: located in Guatemala Department

background.text: Its metropolitan area is also the largest in Central America.
The city is located in a mountain valley called Valle de la Ermita (English: 'Hermitage Valley') in the south-central part of the country.

wd:Q302045.label: Post-Soviet states
wd:Q302045.description: states established following the disestablishment of the Soviet Union
wd:Q302045.overview: The post-Soviet states, also referred to as the former Soviet Union or the former Soviet republics, are the independent sovereign states that emerged/re-emerged from the dissolution of the Soviet Union in 1991. Prior to their independence, they existed as Union Republics, which were the top-level constituents of the Soviet Union.

facts.label: is a
facts.quote: Post-Soviet states: is a cultural region

facts.label: is a
facts.quote: Post-Soviet states: is a geopolitical group

background.text: There are 15 post-Soviet states in total: Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Estonia, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Latvia, Lithuania, Moldova, Russia, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Ukraine, and Uzbekistan.
In Russia, the term "near abroad" (Russian: ближнее зарубежье, romanized: bližneye zarubežye) is sometimes used to refer to the post-Soviet states other than Russia.

wd:Q66458647.label: European Union tax haven blacklist
wd:Q66458647.description: European Commission tool against tax avoidance
wd:Q66458647.overview: The European Union tax haven blacklist, officially the EU list of non-cooperative tax jurisdictions, is a tool of the European Union (EU) that lists tax havens. It is used by the Member States to tackle external risks of tax abuse and unfair tax competition.

facts.label: is a
facts.quote: European Union tax haven blacklist: is a blacklist

facts.label: is a
facts.value: Legal Act of the European Union
facts.quote: European Union tax haven blacklist: is a Legal Act of the European Union

background.text: It was adopted for the first time in 2017 as a response to tax avoidance in the EU, screening 92 countries.
It is managed by the Code of Conduct Group for Business Taxation and monitored by the European Commission (EC).

wd:Q48.label: Asia
wd:Q48.description: part of terrestrial continent, mainly in the northeastern quadrant
wd:Q48.overview: Asia (  AY-zhə, UK also  AY-shə) is the largest continent in the world by both land area and population. It covers an area of more than 44 million square kilometres, about 30% of Earth's total land area and 8% of Earth's total surface area.

facts.label: is a
facts.quote: Asia: is a part of the world

background.text: The continent, which has long been home to the majority of the human population, was the site of many of the first civilisations.
Its estimated 4.8 billion people in 2025 constituted approximately 59% of the world's population.

wd:Q5401.label: Eurasia
wd:Q5401.description: continental landmass comprising Europe and Asia
wd:Q5401.overview: Eurasia ( yoor-AY-zhə, also UK:  -⁠shə), is the largest continental area on Earth, comprising all of Europe and Asia. According to some models of the world, physio-graphically, Eurasia is a single continent.

background.text: The concept of Europe and Asia as distinct continents dates back to antiquity, and is largely cultural, but their borders have historically been subject to change.
For example, the ancient Greeks originally included Africa in Asia but classified Europe as separate land.

wd:Q1054379.label: Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology
wd:Q1054379.overview: The Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (文部科学省, Monbu-kagaku-shō; lit. 'Ministry of Letters and Science'; MEXT) is one of the eleven ministries of Japan that compose part of the executive branch of the government of Japan.

wd:Q1490.label: Tokyo
wd:Q1490.description: capital and largest city of Japan
wd:Q1490.overview: Tokyo, officially the Tokyo Metropolis, is the capital and most populous city of Japan. The population of the city proper was over 14 million as of 2023.

facts.label: is a
facts.quote: Tokyo: is a capital of Japan (since 1869)

background.text: The Greater Tokyo Area, which includes Tokyo and parts of six neighboring prefectures, is the third-most populous metropolitan area in the world, with 33 million residents as of 2025.
Lying at the head of Tokyo Bay, Tokyo is part of the Kantō region, on the central coast of Honshu, Japan's largest island.

wd:Q17.label: Japan
wd:Q17.overview: Japan is an island country in East Asia. Located in the Pacific Ocean off the northeast coast of the Asian mainland, it is bordered to the west by the Sea of Japan, the Sea of Okhotsk in the north, and the East China Sea in the south.

background.text: The Japanese archipelago consists of four major islands alongside over 14,000 smaller islands.

Japan is divided into 47 administrative prefectures and eight traditional regions, and around 75% of its terrain is mountainous and heavily forested, concentrating its agriculture and highly urbanized population along its eastern coastal plains.

wd:Q1634011.label: International Astronautical Federation
wd:Q1634011.overview: The International Astronautical Federation (IAF) is an international space advocacy organization based in Paris, and founded in 1951 as a non-governmental organization to establish a dialogue between scientists around the world and to lay the information for international space cooperation. It has over 390 members from 68 countries across the world.

facts.label: is a
facts.quote: International Astronautical Federation: is a non-governmental organization

background.text: They are drawn from space agencies, companies, universities, professional associations, museums, government organizations and learned societies.
The IAF organizes the annual International Astronautical Congress (IAC).

wd:Q126379.label: Consultative Committee for Space Data Systems
wd:Q126379.description: coordinator of data standards for space communication
wd:Q126379.overview: The Consultative Committee for Space Data Systems (CCSDS) was founded in 1982 for governmental and quasi-governmental space agencies to discuss and develop standards for space data and information systems. Currently composed of "eleven member agencies, twenty-eight observer agencies, and over 140 industrial associates," the CCSDS works to support collaboration and interoperability between member agencies through the

background.text: According to the organisation's website, more than 1000 space missions have utilized data and systems standards created by CCSDS.
The activities of the CCSDS are organized around six topic areas and composed of many working groups within the overall Collaborative Working Group Environment (CWE).

wd:Q1865.label: Kuala Lumpur
wd:Q1865.description: federal territory and capital city of Malaysia
wd:Q1865.overview: Kuala Lumpur (KL), officially the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur, is the capital city and a federal territory of Malaysia. It is the most populous city in the country, covering an area of 243 km2 (94 sq mi) with a population of 2,111,536 as of 2026.

facts.label: is a
facts.quote: Kuala Lumpur: is a federal territory of Malaysia

facts.label: is a
facts.quote: Kuala Lumpur: is a big city

background.text: Greater Kuala Lumpur, which itself includes the Klang Valley, is an urban agglomeration of 8.81 million people as of 2024.
It is among the fastest growing metropolitan regions in Southeast Asia, in terms of both population and economic development.

wd:Q182378.label: Putrajaya
wd:Q182378.description: seat of government and administrative centre of Malaysia
wd:Q182378.overview: Putrajaya (Malay pronunciation: [ˌputraˈd͡ʒaja, ˌputrəˈd͡ʒajə] ), officially the Federal Territory of Putrajaya (Malay: Wilayah Persekutuan Putrajaya), is the administrative centre of Malaysia. The seat of the federal government of Malaysia was shifted in 1999 from Kuala Lumpur to Putrajaya because of overcrowding and congestion in the capital, followed by the seat of the national judiciary in 2003.

facts.label: is a
facts.quote: Putrajaya: is a federal territory of Malaysia

background.text: Kuala Lumpur remains Malaysia's national capital city per the federal constitution and continues to serve as the seat of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong and the Parliament of Malaysia, as well as the nation's premier commercial and financial hub.

Conceived in the 1990s by Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad and Kuala Lumpur mayor Elyas Omar, Putrajaya was designed as a modern greenfield administrative capital emphasizing digital communications, sustainable urban planning, and networked e-government.

wd:Q7768.label: ASEAN
wd:Q7768.description: international organisation of Southeast Asian countries
wd:Q7768.overview: The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN, ) is an intergovernmental forum of all 11 states in Southeast Asia. ASEAN primarily focuses on Southeast Asian economic development, peaceful coexistence and adherence to international norms.

background.text: ASEAN operates on the principle of consensus and respecting national sovereignty, meaning that ASEAN as a whole cannot force another member state to change its domestic laws.
ASEAN has a population of more than 680 million people and a purchasing power parity-adjusted gross domestic product (GDP) of around 6.3% global GDP.

wd:Q72829598.label: Latin America and the Caribbean
wd:Q72829598.overview: Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC) is a geopolitical and cultural region encompassing the Americas south of the contiguous United States. It includes all countries and territories in the Americas but the United States, Canada, Greenland, Bermuda and Saint Pierre and Miquelon (Northern America).

facts.label: continent
facts.quote: Latin America and the Caribbean: continent Americas

background.text: It covers an extensive region, extending from The Bahamas and Mexico in the north to Argentina and Chile in the south.
In comparison to Latin America, LAC also includes countries in Central America, South America, and the Caribbean where predominantly non-Latin languages—i.e.

wd:Q155.label: Brazil
wd:Q155.overview: Brazil, officially the Federative Republic of Brazil, is the largest country in South America. It is also the world's fifth-largest country by area and the seventh-largest by population, with over 214 million people.

background.text: Brazil is a federation composed of 26 states and a Federal District, which hosts the capital, Brasília.
Its most populous city is São Paulo, followed by Rio de Janeiro.

wd:Q414.label: Argentina
wd:Q414.overview: Argentina, officially the Argentine Republic, is a country in the far south of South America. It covers an area of 2,780,085 km2 (1,073,397 mi2), making it the second-largest country in South America after Brazil, the fourth-largest country in the Americas, and the eighth-largest country in the world.

background.text: Argentina shares the bulk of the Southern Cone with Chile to the west, and is also bordered by Bolivia and Paraguay to the north, Brazil to the northeast, Uruguay and the South Atlantic Ocean to the east, and the Drake Passage to the south.
Argentina is a federal state divided into twenty-three provinces, and one autonomous city, which is the federal capital and largest city of the nation, Buenos Aires.

wd:Q750.label: Bolivia
wd:Q750.overview: Bolivia, officially the Plurinational State of Bolivia, is a landlocked country located in central South America. Its geography primarily consists of an Andean region to the west and tropical lowlands to the east and north.

background.text: The country has a diverse environment, including the vast Amazonian plain, the Gran Chaco, temperate valleys, the high-altitude Altiplano plateau, snow-capped peaks, and mountains, encompassing a wide range of climates and biomes across its regions and cities.
It includes part of the Pantanal, the largest tropical wetland in the world, along its eastern border.

wd:Q828.label: Americas
wd:Q828.description: North America and South America taken together as a single continent or landmass
wd:Q828.overview: The Americas, sometimes collectively called America, are a landmass comprising the totality of North America and South America. When viewed as a single continent, the Americas are the second largest continent by area after Asia and the third largest continent by population.

facts.label: is a
facts.quote: Americas: is a part of the world

background.text: The Americas make up most of the land in Earth's Western Hemisphere and constitute the "New World", in contrast to the "Old World" of Afro-Eurasia.
Along with their associated islands, the Americas cover 8% of Earth's total surface area and 28.4% of its land area.

wd:Q538.label: Insular Oceania
wd:Q538.description: geographic region comprising Melanesia, Micronesia and Polynesia
wd:Q538.overview: Oceania is a geographical region – or, in certain classifications, one of the world’s continents – including Australasia, Melanesia, Micronesia, and Polynesia. Spanning the Eastern and Western hemispheres, at the centre of the water hemisphere, Oceania is estimated to have a land area of about 9,000,000 square kilometres (3,500,000 sq mi) and a population of around 46.3 million as of 2024, including Australia but exc

background.text: When compared against other continental land areas, Oceania is the smallest and the second-least populated after Antarctica.
It is home to Earth's third-largest remaining area of tropical rainforest, which covers much of the island of New Guinea.

wd:Q61.label: Washington, D.C.
wd:Q61.description: capital city of the United States of America
wd:Q61.overview: Washington, D.C., officially the District of Columbia and commonly shortened to  Washington, or DC, is the capital city of the United States, and its only federal district. The city stands on the north-east bank of the Potomac River, across from the state of Virginia, surrounded by Maryland to its north, east, and south.

facts.quote: Washington, D.C.: is a city in the United States

facts.label: is a

facts.label: located in

background.text: The district was named for Columbia, the female personification of the American nation, through which human form and attributes are applied to the United States.
"Washington" is a more recent addition to the city's common name, and is from the name of George Washington, the first U.S. president.

wd:Q123705.label: neighborhood
wd:Q123705.description: geographically localized community within a larger city, town or suburb
wd:Q123705.overview: A neighbourhood (Commonwealth English) or neighborhood (American English) is a geographically localized community within a larger town, city, suburb or rural area, sometimes consisting of a single street and the buildings lining it. Neighbourhoods are often social communities with considerable face-to-face interaction among members.

facts.label: is a
facts.quote: neighborhood: is a classification of human settlements

background.text: Researchers have not agreed on an exact definition, but the following may serve as a starting point: "Neighbourhood is generally defined spatially as a specific geographic area and functionally as a set of social networks.

Neighbourhoods, then, are the spatial units in which face-to-face social interactions occur—the personal settings and situations where residents seek to realise common values, socialise youth, and maintain effective social control."

wd:Q191.label: Estonia
wd:Q191.overview: Estonia, officially the Republic of Estonia, is a country in the Baltic region of Northern Europe. It is bordered to the north by the Gulf of Finland across from Finland, to the west by the Baltic Sea across from Sweden, to the south by Latvia, and to the east by Russia.

background.text: The territory of Estonia consists of the mainland, the larger islands of Saaremaa and Hiiumaa, and over 2,300 other islands and islets on the east coast of the Baltic Sea.
Its capital city of Tallinn, along with the city of Tartu, are the country's two largest urban areas.

wd:Q211.label: Latvia
wd:Q211.overview: Latvia, officially the Republic of Latvia, is a country in the Baltic region of northern Europe. It is one of the three Baltic states, along with Estonia to the north and Lithuania to the south.

facts.label: is a
facts.quote: Latvia: is a country bordering the Baltic Sea

background.text: It borders Russia to the east and Belarus to the southeast and shares a maritime border with Sweden to the west.
Latvia covers an area of 64,573 km2 (24,932 sq mi), with a population of 1.83 million.

wd:Q37.label: Lithuania
wd:Q37.overview: Lithuania, officially the Republic of Lithuania, is a country in the Baltic region of Europe. It is one of three Baltic states and lies on the eastern shore of the Baltic Sea, bordered by Latvia to the north, Belarus to the east and south, Poland to the south, and the Russian semi-exclave of Kaliningrad Oblast to the southwest, with a maritime border with Sweden to the west.

background.text: Lithuania covers an area of 65,300 km2 (25,200 sq mi), and has a population of 2.9 million.
Its capital and largest city is Vilnius; other major cities include Kaunas, Klaipėda, Šiauliai and Panevėžys.

wd:Q529012.label: Cabinet of Japan
wd:Q529012.description: executive branch of the government of Japan
wd:Q529012.overview: The Cabinet of Japan (内閣, Naikaku; [naꜜi.ka.kɯ]) is the chief executive body of the government of Japan. It consists of the prime minister, who is appointed by the Emperor after being nominated by the National Diet, in addition to up to seventeen other members, called ministers of state.

facts.label: is a
facts.quote: Cabinet of Japan: is a executive branch

facts.label: parent organisation
facts.quote: Cabinet of Japan: parent organisation Government of Japan

background.text: The current cabinet, the Second Takaichi cabinet, was formed on 18 February 2026 and is led by Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi.
The country has had a Liberal Democratic Party-led majority government since 2026.

wd:Q8056299.label: Yoshitami Kameoka
wd:Q8056299.overview: Yoshitami Kameoka is a former Japanese politician of the Liberal Democratic Party, who served as a member of the House of Representatives in the Diet (national legislature). A native of Tochigi Prefecture and graduate of Waseda University, he was elected for the first time in 2005 after unsuccessful runs in 2000 and 2003.

wd:Q11360463.label: Michiko Ueno
wd:Q11360463.overview: Michiko Ueno is a Japanese politician. She is a member of the House of Councillors, the upper house of the National Diet of Japan.

wd:Q2.label: Earth
wd:Q2.description: third planet from the Sun in the Solar System
wd:Q2.overview: Earth is the third planet from the Sun and the only astronomical object known to harbor life. This is made possible by Earth being an ocean world, the only one in the Solar System sustaining liquid surface water.

facts.label: is a
facts.value: inner planet of the Solar System
facts.quote: Earth: is a inner planet of the Solar System

background.text: Almost all of Earth's water is contained in its ocean, which covers 70.8% of Earth's crust.
The remaining 29.2% of Earth's crust is dry land, which is predominantly located within Earth's land hemisphere in the form of continental landmasses.

wd:Q27527.label: Afro-Eurasia
wd:Q27527.description: major landmass on Earth consisting of Africa, Asia and Europe
wd:Q27527.overview: Afro-Eurasia (also known as Afroeurasia, and Eurafrasia) is a landmass, occasionally described as a supercontinent, comprising the continents of Africa, Asia, and Europe. The terms are compound words of the names of its constituent parts.

background.text: Afro-Eurasia has also been called the "Old World", in contrast to the "New World" referring to the Americas plus sometimes Oceania and Antarctica.
Afro-Eurasia encompasses 85,135,000 km2 (32,871,000 sq mi), 57% of the world's land area, and has a population of approximately 6.7 billion people, roughly 86% of the world population.

wd:Q27231.label: East Asia
wd:Q27231.overview: East Asia is a geocultural region of Asia. It includes China, Japan, Mongolia, North Korea, South Korea, and Taiwan, plus two special administrative regions of China: Hong Kong and Macau.

background.text: The economies of China, Japan, South Korea, and Taiwan are among the world's largest, fastest-growing, and most prosperous.
East Asia borders North Asia to the north, Southeast Asia to the south, South Asia to the southwest, and Central Asia to the west.

wd:Q11708.label: Southeast Asia
wd:Q11708.overview: Southeast Asia is the geographical south-eastern subregion of Asia, consisting of the regions that are situated south of China, east of the Indian subcontinent, and northwest of mainland Australia, which is a part of Oceania. Southeast Asia is bordered to the north by East Asia, to the west by South Asia and the Bay of Bengal, to the east by Oceania and the Pacific Ocean, and to the south by Australia and the Indian

background.text: Apart from the British Indian Ocean Territory and two out of 26 atolls of Maldives in South Asia, Maritime Southeast Asia is the only other subregion of Asia that lies partly within the Southern Hemisphere.
Mainland Southeast Asia is entirely in the Northern Hemisphere.

wd:Q27275.label: Central Asia
wd:Q27275.overview: Central Asia is a region of Asia consisting of Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, and most of Kazakhstan. The countries as a group are also colloquially referred to as the "-stans" as all have names ending with the Persian suffix "-stan" (meaning 'land') in both respective native languages and most other languages.

facts.label: is a
facts.quote: Central Asia: is a cultural region

background.text: The region is bounded by the Caspian Sea to the southwest, European Russia to the northwest, China and Mongolia to the east, Iran and Indian subcontinent to the south, and Siberia to the north.
Together, the five Central Asian countries have a total population of around 76 million.
